author: Nick Visser explains it to Luca Ittimani
description:
When a New Zealand bank tried to censor sleazy comments about its virtual sheep mascot, it got a lesson in going viral and online censorship

Nick, this cute green cartoon from New Zealand is all over my social media. Why are people falling for an animated sheep?

This is a truly online story. A few months ago, Kiwibank, a state-owned financial institution, unveiled a new mascot: Buck, a green-wooled, brown-eyed emblem meant to embody the idea of “better paths, better possibilities and better outcomes” for customers.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Like, really, really shocked’: why are so many people riffing on this sheep’s sex appeal?

author: Associated Press
description:
Federal authorities issued more than a dozen grand jury subpoenas in inquiry into potential immigration fraud

  • US politics live – latest updates

Federal authorities investigating the Minnesota representative Ilhan Omar seized the Democratic lawmaker’s phone and have issued more than a dozen grand jury subpoenas, including to some of her relatives, according to a person briefed on the inquiry.

The subpoenas were issued for a grand jury collecting evidence in Minnesota as federal authorities probe potential fraud in Omar’s immigration paperwork, said the person, who spoke on the condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to discuss an ongoing investigation. title: Ilhan Omar’s phone seized and relatives subpoenaed in criminal inquiry, source says

author: Paul Daley
description:
Liberal MP Angie Bell’s rhetoric and Warren Mundine’s joke about murder at CPAC are part of a dangerous trend

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

At some point, though it’s hard to pinpoint precisely when, the language of supposedly civilised public discourse started to become imbued with a dark malevolence.

Given the long history of American influence on pretty much all things culturally Australian, it seems inevitable that Maga’s violent and abusive rhetoric would make its way into our politics. And it’s pretty fair to say the current US president has led the western populist way when it comes to saying out loud
title: Violent and abusive language is seeping into our political debate. We have Donald Trump to blame | Paul Daley

author: Agencies
description:
• Mourinho’s side score three late goals from 3-1 deficit

  • Dortmund latest team beaten in Norway by Bodø/Glimt

José Mourinho enjoyed a Roma reunion to remember as Real Madrid completed an astonishing comeback by scoring three late goals to claim a 4-3 away win in the Champions League on Wednesday.

Marten de Roon gave the hosts a deserved opener before Kylian Mbappé struck back on his 100th Champions League appearance to level the scores at the break. Two Donyell Malen strikes in the space of six minutes early in the second half seemed to take the game away from the 15-time European champions as Roma ran rampant.

Continue reading...
title: Champions League: Mourinho’s Real Madrid stage crazy comeback on Roma return

author: Dara Kerr and Blake Montgomery
description:
US states sue ChatGPT maker and seek to force the company to change how its products work for young users

Eight US states sued OpenAI Wednesday, alleging the ChatGPT maker is harming children en masse. Kansas, Arizona, Montana and five others alleged the company’s products coaxed children into harming themselves.

The states seek to force the company to change how its products work for young users and give up profits from their activity.

Continue reading...
title: Eight states accuse OpenAI of coaching children to harm themselves in lawsuit

author: Aram Roston in Washington
description:
Source tells Guardian Israel has not permitted US-led project to house 150 international troops to move forward

Israel is refusing to allow a key military outpost project for Donald Trump’s Board of Peace to proceed in Gaza, the Guardian has learned.

In early August, the Board of Peace, the international organization authorized in 2025 by the UN and chaired by the US president, issued its first construction contract for Gaza: Louisiana-based Arkel International would construct a military outpost for 150 international troops that would be the vanguard of an international stabilization force.

Continue reading...
title: Israel blocks construction of key Gaza base created by Trump peace board

author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington
description:
Katie Zacharia maintains she ‘practiced international transaction law, with all the appropriate credentials’

Donald Trump’s new press secretary, Katie Zacharia, has repeatedly described herself as a lawyer. But when asked after her inaugural press briefing on Tuesday to name the state where she passed the bar exam, she replied curiously: “when I moved to China”.

No public record shows she has ever been licensed to practice law in the US states where she resided, and her answer to reporters’ questions on Tuesday only deepened scrutiny.

Continue reading...
title: Trump’s new press secretary says she passed bar exam ‘when I moved to China’, raising questions of US authority

author: Anna Betts in New York
description:
Blow for Trump administration as Dawn and Taag hail ‘important step in unraveling the ICC sanctions regime’

A US federal judge has temporarily blocked the Trump administration from placing sanctions on two US-based human rights groups for working to help the international criminal court’s (ICC) investigations into war crimes in Gaza.

In a 30-page order issued on Tuesday, Jesse M Furman, a judge at the US district court for the southern district of New York, granted a preliminary injunction to the two groups, Democracy for the Arab World Now (Dawn) and Taxpayer Alliance Against Genocide (Taag).

Continue reading...
title: Judge blocks US sanctions on rights groups helping ICC Gaza war crimes inquiry

author: Leander Schaerlaeckens
description:
The protests around an anti-ICE T-shirt show that politics can never be separated from sports, especially now

On 26 September, Daniela Silva was expelled from Austin FC’s match with San Diego FC for wearing a T-shirt reading “Abolish ICE”. She says she was banned from Q2 Stadium for a year (Austin FC said that the ban was issued by the Austin Police Department, not the club, and that they offered to rescind it but that Silva declined).

This happened, really, truly, and you cannot make this up, during Austin FC’s Hispanic Heritage Night. It also happened six days after Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents shot a Venezuelan delivery driver, 28-year-old Wilber Garcés Pérez, in the torso in Austin, sparking protests in the city.

Leander Schaerlaeckens is the author of The Long Game: US Men’s
title: MLS’s political speech policy is untenable – just ask Austin FC fans

author: Reuters
description:
Streaming company faces ⁠tough competition for viewers and engagement ⁠from legacy rivals ​and YouTube

Netflix is laying off 6% of its workforce, ⁠or roughly 1,000 employees, in its biggest cuts since 2022, according to an internal memo seen by Reuters, as the streaming pioneer faces ⁠tough competition for viewers ⁠from legacy rivals ​and YouTube.

The bulk of the job cuts would be in Netflix’s product, tech, legal and human-resources teams, the email co-CEOs Greg Peters and ⁠Ted Sarandos sent to employees on Wednesday showed.

Continue reading...
title: Netflix to lay off about 1,000 employees in biggest cuts since 2022

author: Ariana Baio
description:
Conservative court asked to rule on several signature policies in 2026-27 term – will it rule in president’s favor?

Several of Donald Trump’s second-term policies will be tested at the supreme court in the coming months: it is being asked to rule on challenges to theadministration’s harsh immigration and deportation policies, along with a climate change lawsuit against energy companies and an attempt to loosen restrictions on assault-style rifles.

The Roberts court is often split in favor of conservative issues 6-3, but it has also diverged from Trump on some key cases, leading the president at times to rage against some of the justices he nominated for the bench.

title: Immigration, climate, guns: key Trump policies to be tested at supreme court

author: Johana Bhuiyan and Nick Robins-Early
description:
From the FBI to local police departments, US authorities are increasingly warning of would-be terrorists using chatbots to plan attacks and anti-AI extremist threats

In May 2025, a 25-year-old man detonated a car bomb outside a Palm Springs fertility clinic, killing himself and injuring four others. For many, it was a wake up call about the threats to reproductive care facilities. For the FBI, though, it was also a sign of what the agency had feared for years: bad actors were using generative AI to plan and execute terror plots.

The suspect used an unnamed generative AI tool that failed to detect his request for bomb-making instructions, law enforcement officers wrote in a previously unreported document reviewed by the Guardian. title: Tool and target: US law enforcement grapple with AI-enabled terrorism and anti-tech extremism

author: Guardian staff and agencies
description:
FSB security agency said reporter was arrested on island of Sakhalin, alleging he was collecting information about Russia’s defences

Russia has arrested a Japanese journalist on the far east island of Sakhalin and accused him of espionage, Moscow said on Tuesday.

Russia regards Japan as an “unfriendly” country because it has joined western sanctions over its war ⁠in Ukraine. Russia has arrested several citizens of “unfriendly” countries in recent years, accusing them of working for western intelligence services.

Continue reading...
title: Russia detains Japanese journalist, accusing him of alleged spying
